raw_case_text:
A 10-year-old, right-handed, Chinese patient presented for clinical evaluation of a 2-week history characterized by impaired concentration, irritable mood, slurred speech, and slow, cautious gait. There was no recent history of an infectious disorder. The neurologic examination revealed bradypsychia, dysarthria, and downbeat nystagmus. The patient had dysmetria and dysdiadochokinesia. Tandem gait showed frank ataxia. Romberg's sign was negative.
Initial investigation showed normal blood cell count, lactic acid levels, d-dimer assays, and hepatic and renal function tests. Serology for hepatitis C and HIV type 1 and 2 were negative. A lumbar puncture revealed an opening pressure of 16.5 cm/H2O. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) protein was 0.3 g/L (0.15-0.45 g/L), lactic dehydrogenase was 40.5 U/L ( <= 70 U/L), granular leukocytes were 30 x 106/L (0-5 x 106/L), and glucose and chloride levels were normal. Ziehl-Neelsen staining for acid-fast bacilli and Cryptococcus neoformans smear test in the CSF were negative. We used tissue-based assay by indirect immunofluorescence in fixed rat brain slices to screen for antibodies reacting with central nervous system antigens. Then, we used a commercially available cell-based assay to check for interest antibodies. Anti-Homer-3 antibody was positive in the CSF (1:1) (Figure 1) cell-based assay; however, the test was negative in the serum. Other antibodies such as anti-NMDAR, anti-AMPA1, anti-AMPA2, anti-CASPR2, anti-DPPX, anti-DRD2, anti-GlyR, anti-GAD65, anti-GABAB, anti-IgLON5, anti-LGI1, anti-mGlutR1, and anti-mGlutR5, as well as onconeural antibodies, were negative; however, low titers of anti-voltage gated calcium channel antibodies (VGCC-antibodies) were found in the serum: 41 pmol/L (normal value <= 30 pmol/L).
A detailed ultrasound examination of abdominal and pelvic structures was normal without evidence of tumor and a chest X-ray was unremarkable.
Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed hyperintensities in both cerebellar hemispheres and vermis in FLAIR and T2-weighted (T2W) sequences (Figures 2A,B).
Initial treatment was carried out with intravenous boluses of methylprednisolone (1 g per day for 5 days), followed by oral prednisolone at decreasing doses for 15 days. No improvement was observed on day 10; for that reason, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) was offered, but the patient's parents initially declined for personal reasons.
As no improvement in cognitive and motor condition was observed in the following weeks, the patient's parents accepted treatment with IVIg 1 month after the initial assessment. Slow but progressive clinical improvement was noticed with normalization of cognitive impairment and cerebellar syndrome a year later March 1, 2022, when only mild dysarthria was noticed, a score of 1 on the modified Rankin Scale was registered at that time. Follow-up MRI showed mild cerebellar atrophy (Figures 2C,D).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 10-year-old right-handed Chinese patient presented with a 2-week history of impaired concentration, irritable mood, slurred speech, and a slow, cautious ataxic gait.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the 2 weeks prior to evaluation, the previously healthy child developed progressive difficulty concentrating, irritability, dysarthria, and a cautious, unsteady gait without any preceding infectious illness.
subjective.past_medical_history: No recent infectious disorder or significant past medical history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for impaired concentration, irritable mood, slurred speech, and gait unsteadiness.

objective.physical_examination: Neurological examination revealed bradypsychia, dysarthria, downbeat nystagmus, appendicular dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia, frank tandem gait ataxia, and a negative Romberg's sign.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC, lactic acid, D-dimer, hepatic and renal function tests, HCV and HIV-1/2 serologies, chest X-ray, and abdominal/pelvic ultrasounds were all normal or negative. Serum anti-voltage-gated calcium channel (VGCC) antibody was mildly elevated at 41 pmol/L (normal: <=30 pmol/L).
objective.advanced_workup: Brain MRI demonstrated T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the bilateral cerebellar hemispheres and vermis (evolving to mild cerebellar atrophy at 1-year follow-up). Lumbar puncture showed opening pressure 16.5 cmH2O, CSF WBC 30 x 10^6/L (normal: 0-5 x 10^6/L), normal protein 0.3 g/L (0.15-0.45 g/L), normal LDH 40.5 U/L (<=70 U/L), normal glucose and chloride, and negative CSF Ziehl-Neelsen AFB stain and Cryptococcus neoformans smear. Rat brain indirect immunofluorescence and cell-based assay identified positive CSF anti-Homer-3 antibodies (titer 1:1; serum negative), while anti-NMDAR, AMPA1/2, CASPR2, DPPX, DRD2, GlyR, GAD65, GABAB, IgLON5, LGI1, mGluR1/5, and onconeural antibodies were negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of pediatric anti-Homer-3 antibody-associated autoimmune cerebellitis, confirmed by positive CSF anti-Homer-3 cell-based assay (1:1), bilateral cerebellar/vermian T2/FLAIR hyperintensities on MRI, and CSF pleocytosis (30 x 10^6/L) after excluding tuberculous and Cryptococcus neoformans meningitis. After showing no improvement at day 10 following pulsed IV methylprednisolone (1 g/day for 5 days) and a 15-day oral prednisolone taper, administration of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) 1 month after initial assessment led to progressive cognitive and motor normalization at 1-year follow-up (modified Rankin Scale score 1 with only mild residual dysarthria).
